review_notes: Reviewed the current top-level proposal, not merely the older proposal embedded in context. All six proposed writes are supported by canonical source and target owned subjects. No replacement proposal or mutation is supplied.

Read both complete owned files in canonical and rendered form, all five subject pages, both link pages, the complete 144-line proposal, the complete 43-line functionality document, all 615 lines of the fact ledger, and all 316 lines of the link ledger.

Independently checked the platform predicate and floor-skip updater, airborne initialization and comparison-based clamping, RETURN_IF expansion, active Pass callback association, Reflector continuation callers, Guard caller, Squat countdown consumer, delegated entry path, Fall routing, airborne physics, and cited Mewtwo/Sheik recovery branches.

The proposal correctly repairs input.lstick.y to input.lstick[0].y and held_inputs to held_buttons[0]. It preserves branch priority, exact transition ordering, and the fact that floor_skip is copied after the motion-state call.

RETURN_IF evaluates each reached condition once and returns on nonzero. This supports the proposed canonical arbitration description, but does not independently establish every predicate's accepted action or false-return side effects.

Acceptance does not promote deferred baseline claims to proved facts. Additional independent deferrals below cover literal interpretations of support/grounded status, universal clamping, ordinary airborne outcomes, and unverified callee semantics. None requires an additional write to make the six proposed changes accurate.

Rendered names were treated as hypotheses. The duplicated ftCo_Pass_CheckInput alias remains unresolved; section layout, parameter register placement, and pass/squat compiled storage layout were not inferred from source spelling.

The functionality document accurately distinguishes local behavior from external lifetime and configuration obligations. Its finite nonnegative clamp-bound discussion must also be read with its explicit qualification that NaN velocity is not repaired.
